subdivision_of_building: Front Ground floor - attached to the shop
description:
The development conducted was for the removal of two damaged air conditioner units with safety issues enclosed in a broken box. This was replaced with the installation of two compressor units and a new wooden box at 125 Praed Street. This was completed on the 4th of July 2025.

These changes were made due to two refrigerator units inside the shop being rendered inoperable. Because of connections to the outside units, the fridges were not cooling properly. Eventually the units broke down. As these drinks were not cooling, customers became frustrated at having warm drinks in summer weather. We were losing customers and business because of this issue. 

We further faced issues with the company we hired to remove and replace the fridges. After removal, it took them a few days to come out and complete the job after we continually expressed the need to keep the shop clean and replace the all the units. 

The were removed on 2nd of July. There was an issue with removing and replacing them due to the existing box. This box did not have a door and was connected by some loose nails. Further safety issues appeared as a result of this deteriorating box, for instance, the jagged edges of the box from the metal wire were incredibly sharp and sticking out. 

In order to remove the units, the box enclosed needed to be removed completely. Unfortunately, because of its condition, it could not be fixed back together as the box was unfit for further use due to its integrity. Therefore, with the installation of the new refrigerator units, a new box to enclose was put in. 

Furthermore, the Praed Street area has witnessed mounting thefts and criminal activity. Even on the day of removal we had two attempted thefts. 
This increased the urgency of the matter as two compressor units placed by the shop, with no protection, would have been prone to thefts. To prevent this, a new box needed to be constructed to ensure the proper function of the cooler units inside. The box would be able to protect the units from harsh weather damage. Due to the summer, and the weather there was a matter of urgency to change the cooling units. 

Lastly, we had no idea permission needed to be obtained from the Council, or that the Council even needed to be informed about the change of the box and compressor units. The letter we received described the units as “air conditioners.” This is false. These are NOT air conditioning units, but instead compressors. 

Now that we have received this letter, we understand the colour of the box must be green, to correspond with the theme of the shop. We have now painted this box green and will upload a photo. These changes were necessary as the shop cannot function without coolers, and the enclosure was necessary for security and safety.
